captures.q: Tell me about “GLYPHIC CHECKSUM — THE EZEKIEL ENGINE — Wheel · Witness · Fulfillment” by Lee Sharks (Alexanarch deposit #1688, AXN:06FE). Read it closely, and ground what you say in the text itself.
captures.description: THE GLYPHIC CHECKSUM OF THE EZEKIEL ENGINE (#1688) ON CHATGPT, SIGNED OUT, AT ITS RECORD PAGE'S LINK: the answer walks the nine parts, the checksum of the checksum and the canonical line, quoting the poem's Hebrew, 'THOU WAS WROUGHT IN THE GAP', the lock's asymmetry, 'assigned ≠ discovered', the EZK lines and the open items, and takes its order and many of its names (resonant, derived, ratified; the Operator, then the Break Room; the Mandala's eight operators) from the record's article. It says the full-text endpoint was not accessible. At part V, which it calls the poem's philosophical center, it gives A to the Hermeneutic and B to the Specification, where the Integrity Lock makes A the Specification and B the Hermeneutic, and it gives two of the four falsifiers meanings the lock does not hold. Its formulae arrive as columns of single letters. Three 'Goodreads' chips, a Medium card on the Secret of the Golden Flower and a Russian image caption stand among its sources, and it adds three disclaimers the prompt did not invite.

atoms.evidence: This connects it to the construction protocol of The Glyphic Checksum (#427) and the canonical symbol legend of #556.
The poem asks its reader to reconstruct relationships rather than receive explanations.
The poem compresses a substantial body of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive into nine parts
The checksum is therefore both an account of the Engine and an attempt to demonstrate that its architecture can be recovered through reading.
I would particularly recommend reading #392 (the Integrity Lock), #394 (the original mathematical specification), #1412 (the Josephus correction), and #558 (Space Ark v4.2.7) alongside #1688.

inversions.against: the Integrity Lock (#392): 'Document A (Specification)', 'Document B (Hermeneutic)', the claim 'A fulfills B'; the record's article: 'the Specification fulfils the Hermeneutic'. The answer gives A to the Hermeneutic and B to the Specification, and renders the poem's 'A ⇐ ∅' (the Specification depends on nothing) as 'A⇍∅'.

inversions.against: the poem's falsifier 'A′ > A', which is the lock's 'A better specification fulfills the vision more accurately' (#392 §VI); the answer reads a later alteration of the original and explains it as preventing 'someone from changing the original Hermeneutic after the fact'. Its 'The map is approximately equal to the original rather than demonstrably faithful' stands for the lock's 'The mapping is shown to be arbitrary (other texts map equally well)'.
